title: Which digits make the biggest and smallest product?
description: The digits two, four, five, eight and zero fill five boxes in a product of a number with one decimal place and another with one decimal place. The video places the digits to make the biggest product, the smallest product, one above one hundred fifty, one nearest one hundred and one nearest five.
teaching_notes: One idea: treat the product as whole numbers with two decimal places put back, then place the biggest digits where they add most to make a big product, and the smallest where they add least to make a small one. Ask the class where the digit eight should go to make the biggest product before any work is shown. Watch for students who put zero in the leading place of the first number.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q10
video_script.why: The child can count the decimal places of a product from the whole number product, and now uses place value to choose digits that make a product big, small or near a target.
video_script.substitution: The boxes are read as a three digit whole number times a two digit whole number, with two decimal places put back, and the digits go where they add most or least.
video_script.anchor: Boxes for two digits, a point and one digit, times one digit, a point and one digit, with the digits 2, 4, 5, 8, 0 and five targets
video_script.payoff_line: Here are the five arrangements and their products

final_answer.spoken: eighty two point zero times five point four is four hundred forty two point eight; forty five point eight times zero point two is nine point one six; twenty eight point zero times five point four is one hundred fifty one point two; twenty point five times four point eight is ninety eight point four; and nine point one six for the one nearest five

maths_rules: boxes: (two digits . one digit) x (one digit . one digit) has 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places, so it is a 3 digit x 2 digit whole number product divided by 100
(a) biggest: 8 in the tens of the first number, 5 in the units of the second, 4 in the tenths of the second (it multiplies a number near 80), 2 and 0 in the rest: 82.0 x 5.4 = 442.8
(b) smallest: second number 0.2, first number 45.8: 45.8 x 0.2 = 9.16
(e) every product is at least 9.16, which is more than 5, so the smallest product is nearest to 5
video_script.design: One idea: read the boxes as whole numbers with two decimal places put back, then place digits by what they add. The boxes and the digits stay on the board all video; the working band takes the five targets one at a time, and the answer beat evaluates the products.
open_questions: The book does not say each digit is used once. Five boxes and five digits, and the worklist answers, show that it is. The video says each digit is used once.
The target above one hundred fifty has many answers. The video gives the one from the worklist and calls it an example.

beats.on_screen: To find: (a) the biggest product (b) the smallest product (c) a product above 150 (d) a product nearest 100 (e) a product nearest 5

marks.find: the five targets are written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to place the digits for each of the five targets.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, biggest: 8 in the tens of the first number, 5 in the units of the second; 4 in the tenths of the second, since it is multiplied by a number near 80; then 2 and 0: 82.0 × 5.4

marks.big: 8 goes in the tens place of the first number and 5 in the units place of the second
marks.four: 4 goes in the tenths place of the second number, with a note: multiplied by a number near 80
marks.rest: 2 and 0 go in the rest and 82.0 × 5.4 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step one, the biggest product. Put the biggest digits in the leftmost places.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Eight goes in the tens place of the first number. Five goes in the units place of the second.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four goes in the tenths place of the second number. That digit is multiplied by a number near eighty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Two and zero fill the rest.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, smallest: second number as small as possible: 0.2; first number from 4, 5, 8: 45.8 × 0.2

marks.second: the second number 0.2 is written, with 0 in the units and 2 in the tenths
marks.first: the first number 45.8 is written from the digits 4, 5, 8

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step two, the smallest product. Make the second number as small as possible.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Zero goes in its units place and two, the smallest digit left, in its tenths place. It is zero point two.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first number is made smallest from four, five and eight. It is forty five point eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, above 150: swap the 8 and the 2 of the biggest: 28.0 × 5.4 = 28 × 5 + 28 × 0.4; 28 × 5 = 140; 28 × 0.4 = 11.2

marks.swap: the 8 and the 2 swap places in 82.0 × 5.4 and 28.0 × 5.4 is written
marks.split: 28 × 5 + 28 × 0.4 is written with 140 and 11.2 under it

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step three, a product above one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>Swap the eight and the two in the biggest one. The first number becomes twenty eight point zero.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Split it as twenty eight times five plus twenty eight times zero point four. That is one hundred forty and eleven point two.

marks.why: the step title is written and 100 is lit
marks.split: 20 × 4.8 and 0.5 × 4.8 are written with 96 and 2.4 under them

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step four, a product nearest to one hundred. Try numbers near twenty times five.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Take twenty point five times four point eight.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Twenty times four point eight is ninety six. Zero point five times four point eight is two point four.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, nearest 5: the smallest product is more than 45 × 0.2 = 9, which is already more than 5; every other product is bigger

marks.why: the step title is written and 5 is lit
marks.small: the smallest product from step 2 is joined to the target 5

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step five, a product nearest to five.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Forty five times zero point two is nine. The smallest product is more than nine, well above five.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Every other product is bigger, so the smallest product is the nearest to five.

marks.ans: the five arrangements and their products are written and boxed
marks.d: 20.5 × 4.8 = 98.4 is lit, with the gap 1.6 from 100

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Here are the five arrangements and their products.
<bookmark mark='a'/>The biggest, eighty two point zero times five point four, is four hundred forty two point eight.
<bookmark mark='b'/>The smallest, forty five point eight times zero point two, is nine point one six.
<bookmark mark='c'/>For above one hundred fifty, take twenty eight point zero times five point four. It is one hundred fifty one point two.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Nearest to one hundred, twenty point five times four point eight, is ninety eight point four. It is one point six away.
<bookmark mark='e'/>Nearest to five is the smallest product again, nine point one six.
